spec.name: sprint42_taker_imbalance_slow_24h_hold_top12
spec.hypothesis: Order-flow imbalance predicts crypto returns at multi-hour to multi-day lags (EFMA 2025). Prior taker_imbalance specs used short holds where T2 costs (~26bp) exceed any edge. A slow-smoothed extreme imbalance with a 24h hold tests the literature's actual horizon, with the cost/edge ratio cut roughly 10x versus 15-min holds. Long-only, one entry per symbol per day.
spec.power_argument: 12 symbols x ~92 validation days, cap 1/day/symbol => <=1104 entries; z>2.5 on 240-min smoothed imbalance is expected to fire ~30-45% of symbol-days, giving ~300-500 validation trades (n>=300 required; if the validator rejects, loosen threshold to 2.0 before freezing). 24h return std ~300bp => min detectable per-trade edge at n=400, t=2 is ~30bp, above the T2 cost floor (~26bp). The criterion can fail under the null (t>=2.0 net of T2 with same-sign research effect); only a large edge is detectable.
